findings.claim: The 'Bossfang receiving service identity: Local operator mode versus delegated remote user/actor must be observable' acceptance scenario has no assigned candidate or build_required entry, so Plan will lack a concrete scope for Bossfang-side identity classification
findings.evidence: Acceptance-scenarios table row 18 maps this to the same disposition as F2/F3, but cand-009 fit_for_gap is 'F2/F3/G7-A common inbound policy independent of downstream receiver inventory' scoped to UAR, and cand-001 fit_for_gap is 'F1/F5: one executor, admission identity, observation and cancellation' focused on UAR's owner/workspace/admission identity. No candidate covers the Bossfang-side classification of an inbound request as service-mode versus delegated-user/actor.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a candidate or build_required entry that explicitly scopes the Bossfang inbound identity classification; either extend cand-009 to cover both boundaries or add a new pattern candidate that names the Bossfang adapter as the authority for service-versus-delegated classification, with an observable (e.g., distinct request-attribution field) Plan can assert against.

findings.claim: The proposed F6 reproduction fixture composition overrides the Assess handoff's 'F6 fixture choice' carry-forward without reconciling the change
findings.evidence: Assess handoff: 'Carry forward original ignored-metadata evidence limits, F6 fixture choice, out-of-scope hook writeback and comparator-only scope'. Analysis F6 section: 'The existing generic test_config disables JWT and therefore cannot be reused unchanged. This is a proposed fixture composition, not an already passing test.' The new composition (in-process Rust integration harness with minted two-JWT fixture) replaces the carried-forward choice without referencing it or explaining the override.
findings.suggested_fix: Either cite the Assess-chosen fixture and explain why it cannot be reused (justifying the override), or defer the fixture composition to Spec/Plan so the carry-forward is respected. If the override is correct, document it as a deliberate change to a carried-forward Assess decision so downstream stages do not re-litigate it.

findings.claim: REMOTE-RESOURCE-SECRET-STORE is named as a blocking capability_gap_id but no candidate covers a remote token vault abstraction; existing storage modules are explicitly disqualified and the candidate set never enumerates the missing category
findings.evidence: cand-010 evidence: 'AES-256-GCM provider-key encryption; not generic MCP refresh-token persistence' and 'Provider-specific scoped key lookup; do not reinterpret its schema as a remote token vault.' build_required entry for G7-B/F4 storage: why_no_candidate 'remote refresh-token schema, tenant scoping, custody and lifecycle are not established.' No candidate explores OS keyring-per-tenant, vault adapter, or KMS-backed envelope as options.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a candidate enumerating the storage-class options considered (OS keyring, vault, KMS) with verdicts on each, so Plan has constraints when the operator later selects the storage adapter. At minimum, name the candidate categories that were excluded and the reason, to keep the missing-category decision explicit rather than implied.

findings.claim: F6 closure alternative 'enforcing-layer evidence' lacks an observable acceptance criterion that Plan can sequence against
findings.evidence: Analysis: 'Plan must keep any session-binding remediation blocked until the production-router matrix produces a recorded failure (or close the gap with enforcing-layer evidence).' The phrase is undefined operationally; no candidate and no build_required entry specify what the enforcing layer is (JWT middleware? routing rule? session-isolation property?) or what evidence is sufficient to close F6 without a recorded reproduction.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the enforcing layer (e.g., UAR /mcp/uar JWT middleware) and the specific test that demonstrates session crossover is denied before session routing. Add a candidate or build_required entry for the enforcing-layer evidence so Plan can sequence F6-REPRODUCTION and the alternative closure path as parallel gates with distinct observables.

findings.claim: The 'Lost submission/retry' acceptance scenario maps to reconciliation after a lost response but the 'conflict on changed payload' test design is not specified
findings.evidence: Acceptance-scenarios table: 'Same admission/epoch and payload; conflict on changed payload; reconcile missing response.' Analysis: 'changing credential material while resending the same admission is not an exact retry.' No build_required entry or candidate describes the test that asserts the conflict-detection behavior when an admission ID is reused with a different payload.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test-design note or build_required entry for the conflict-on-changed-payload behavior so Plan can author a fixture asserting that admission with the same ID but different payload is rejected with a documented error class, not silently treated as the same attempt.
